title: Git lab: commits, branches, merge, conflicts, stash, rebase and git flow
summary: One server with a repository already made for you: ~/workspace with real branches, a merge history, a conflict already resolved, a stash demo, a rebased branch, a finished git-flow release tagged v1.0, and a bare remote at /srv/git/lab.git. Exercise 0 is for beginners: a repository made from nothing, the first commits, diff, undo, a branch, a remote. The other exercises read Git from underneath (commits as objects, branches as files holding one hash, the index) and then practise every operation; ~/reset-git-lab.sh rebuilds the repository when you have changed its history. Ported from qlab's git-lab.

exercises.title: First steps: your first repository
exercises.text: For whoever has never used Git: a repository made from nothing in ~/first-repo, the first commits, a change seen with diff, an undo, a branch merged back, a .gitignore, and a remote to push to and clone from. Nothing here touches ~/workspace; the other exercises then open Git from underneath.

commands: git --version
git config --global --list    # name and e-mail: Git writes them into every commit (set in the lab; elsewhere: git config --global user.name 'Your Name')
mkdir -p ~/first-repo && cd ~/first-repo && git init -b main
git status    # an empty repository: nothing tracked yet
echo 'Shopping list' > list.txt && git status    # list.txt is untracked
git add list.txt && git status    # staged: in the index, ready to commit
git commit -m 'Start the shopping list' && git log --oneline
cd ~/first-repo && echo 'milk' >> list.txt && echo 'bread' >> list.txt
git diff    # what changed since the last commit
git add list.txt && git commit -m 'Add milk and bread'
git log --oneline && git show --stat HEAD
cd ~/first-repo && echo 'oops' >> list.txt && git diff --stat
git restore list.txt && git diff --stat    # the file is back to the last commit
echo 'eggs' >> list.txt && git add list.txt && git restore --staged list.txt && git status --short    # unstaged, the change stays
git commit -am 'Add eggs'    # -a stages every tracked file that changed
cd ~/first-repo && git switch -c weekend    # a new branch, and you are on it
echo 'cake' >> list.txt && git commit -am 'Weekend: cake'
git switch main && cat list.txt    # no cake on main
git merge weekend && cat list.txt && git log --oneline --graph
git branch -d weekend
cd ~/first-repo && echo 'scratch' > notes.tmp && printf '*.tmp\n' > .gitignore && git status --short    # notes.tmp is not even listed
git add .gitignore && git commit -m 'Ignore temporary files'
git init --bare ~/first-remote.git    # a Git server is just a bare repository
cd ~/first-repo && git remote add origin ~/first-remote.git && git push -u origin main
git clone ~/first-remote.git ~/first-clone && git -C ~/first-clone log --oneline
echo 'coffee' >> list.txt && git commit -am 'Add coffee' && git push
git -C ~/first-clone pull && cat ~/first-clone/list.txt
rm -rf ~/first-repo ~/first-remote.git ~/first-clone    # start over any time

exercises.title: Git anatomy
exercises.text: A repository is a .git/ directory: objects, refs, HEAD and config. The lab's working copy is ~/workspace, its remote the bare repository /srv/git/lab.git: the same files, with no working tree beside them.

commands: cd ~/workspace && ls -a .git
git config --global --list    # who commits
git status; git branch
ls /srv/git/lab.git    # a bare repository: .git's contents, nothing checked out

exercises.title: Commits are objects
exercises.text: A commit holds a tree, its parents, an author and a message; the tree lists names and hashes; the blob is the file content and nothing else. A merge commit is simply one with two parents.

commands: cd ~/workspace && git log --oneline --graph --all
git cat-file -p HEAD    # tree, parent(s), author, message
git cat-file -p HEAD^{tree}    # the directory listing
git cat-file -p HEAD:hello.txt    # the blob: bytes, no name
echo 'My notes' > notes.txt && git add notes.txt && git commit -m 'Add notes.txt'
git commit --amend -m 'docs: add notes.txt'    # a new commit, a new hash
git reset --hard HEAD~1    # back as it was

exercises.title: Branches are pointers
exercises.text: A branch is a file with one hash in it; HEAD is a file naming the branch you are on. Creating or deleting one copies nothing.

commands: cd ~/workspace && git branch -a
cat .git/HEAD; cat .git/refs/heads/main
git branch --merged main
git switch -c feature/my-feature && git switch main
git branch -d feature/my-feature

exercises.title: Merge: fast-forward or a merge commit
exercises.text: When main has not moved, merging a branch just moves the pointer (fast-forward); when both sides moved, Git makes a merge commit with two parents. --no-ff forces one.

commands: cd ~/workspace && git log --merges --oneline
git log --oneline --graph main~6..main
git show --stat HEAD~3    # a merge commit: 'Merge:' lists two parents
git switch -c feature/test-merge && echo test > merge-test.txt && git add merge-test.txt && git commit -m 'test: add merge-test.txt'
git switch main && git merge --no-ff feature/test-merge -m 'Merge feature/test-merge'
git log --oneline --graph -4
git reset --hard origin/main && git branch -D feature/test-merge    # undo

exercises.title: Conflicts
exercises.text: Two branches changed the same lines: Git stops and marks the region with <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>>. You choose the content, add it and commit; the merge commit records the resolution.

commands: cd ~/workspace && cat conflict.txt
git log --oneline --grep=resolve
git diff feature/conflict...main -- conflict.txt
git switch -c branch-a && echo 'Version A' > clash.txt && git add clash.txt && git commit -m 'branch-a: clash.txt'
git switch main && echo 'Version B' > clash.txt && git add clash.txt && git commit -m 'main: clash.txt'
git merge branch-a || cat clash.txt    # the markers
echo 'Resolved version' > clash.txt && git add clash.txt && git commit -m 'Merge: resolve clash.txt'
git reset --hard origin/main && git branch -D branch-a    # undo

exercises.title: Stash
exercises.text: git stash shelves uncommitted changes on a stack so you can switch context; pop puts the newest entry back. Stashes never travel to a remote.

commands: cd ~/workspace && git switch feature/stash
echo 'More work in progress' >> wip.txt && git stash push -m 'WIP: my in-progress work'
git status --short; cat wip.txt    # clean: the change is on the stack
git stash list
git stash pop && cat wip.txt    # the change is back
git checkout -- wip.txt && git switch main    # drop the change, leave the branch clean

exercises.title: Remote
exercises.text: origin is the bare repository. push uploads commits, fetch downloads the remote's refs into remotes/origin/* without touching your branches; origin/main is your last record of the remote, not the remote.

commands: cd ~/workspace && git remote -v
git fetch origin && git log --oneline HEAD..origin/main    # on the remote, not here
git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD    # here, not pushed yet
git ls-remote origin
echo pushed > pushed.txt && git add pushed.txt && git commit -m 'Add pushed.txt' && git push origin main
git log --oneline -1 origin/main    # moved with the push
git reset --hard HEAD~1 && git push --force origin main    # undo (your own remote: never force a shared one)

exercises.title: Rebase
exercises.text: rebase replays a branch's commits on top of another: a linear history with no merge commit. feature/stash was rebased onto main's hotfix. Never rebase commits others already have.

commands: cd ~/workspace && git log --oneline feature/stash
git log --merges main..feature/stash --oneline    # none: linear
git log --oneline --graph main feature/stash
git switch -c feature/rebase-demo main~2 && echo 'old base' > rebase-demo.txt && git add rebase-demo.txt && git commit -m 'demo commit'
git rebase main && git log --oneline -3
git switch main && git branch -D feature/rebase-demo

exercises.title: Git flow
exercises.text: A branching model with roles: main for releases, develop for integration, feature/* from develop, release/* merged into both and tagged, hotfix/* from main. The git-flow CLI does the branching, merging, tagging and cleanup.

commands: cd ~/workspace && git flow version
git config --get-regexp gitflow    # stored in .git/config
git tag; git log --oneline --merges main
git log --oneline --graph develop -8
git flow feature start try-me && echo try > try.txt && git add try.txt && git commit -m 'feature/try-me: try.txt'
GIT_MERGE_AUTOEDIT=no git flow feature finish try-me    # merged into develop, branch removed
git log --oneline -2 develop
bash ~/reset-git-lab.sh    # everything back as the lab hands it to you
